inputs.text:
Turn the same person in the reference image into a true 90-degree LEFT profile.
The reference image is the person's original identity photograph. Use it as the authoritative source for identity, facial structure, hair and mole placement. The photographic rendering of this profile must match a clean, softly lit studio portrait of the same person — see PHOTOGRAPHIC RENDERING below.
This is a viewing-angle transformation of the same person, NOT a new character generation and NOT a new portrait design.
Change ONLY the viewing angle from front-facing to a true 90-degree LEFT profile.
Preserve the person's existing appearance as closely as possible while changing the viewpoint.
IDENTITY AND FACIAL STRUCTURE:
Preserve the exact same person, apparent age, facial proportions and facial character from the reference.
Keep the same:
- forehead shape
- brow position
- eyebrow shape and density
- nose structure and natural projection
- lips and mouth shape
- philtrum
- chin shape
- jawline
- cheekbone structure
- face width and length
- hairline
- facial hair
- mole placement
Do not redesign or reinterpret any facial feature.
Do not beautify, idealize, masculinize, feminize, mature, or make the face more conventionally attractive.
The profile must be the natural side view of the exact same face, with the same underlying facial proportions as the reference.
PROFILE ANGLE:
Create a true anatomical 90-degree LEFT profile.
The face should be viewed directly from the left side, not a three-quarter view and not a near-profile.
The visible facial contour should naturally follow:
forehead → brow → nose bridge → nose tip → philtrum → lips → chin → jawline → neck.
Keep the natural relationship between nose projection, lips, chin and jawline.
The nose should have natural, moderate projection consistent with the reference person's actual facial structure.
The lips should remain naturally integrated into the facial contour, without excessive forward projection, excessive fullness, or an artificial lip outline.
The chin should maintain its natural shape and projection from the reference, without becoming unusually long, sharp, pointed, recessed, or oversized.
The jawline should remain naturally refined and consistent with the reference, without becoming excessively angular, square, heavy, or sharply V-shaped.
SKIN AND NECK:
Render the skin clean, healthy and youthful: an intact, even, smooth surface with only fine subtle texture.
The facial skin and neck skin should belong to the same continuous natural skin surface.
Keep the complexion clean, even and naturally photographic.
Use only subtle natural photographic texture.
Do not invent a new skin texture for the profile.
Do not make the profile skin rougher, darker, harder, more granular, more textured or more processed than a clean studio portrait of this person.
The neck should remain clean, smooth and natural, with the same overall skin appearance as the face.
Maintain soft, continuous tonal transitions from the face into the jaw, neck and upper chest.
Do not introduce artificial dark markings, dark lines, graphic wrinkles, grooves, scratches, scars, or other unnatural surface patterns on the neck.
Do not create a separate or differently textured neck.
The skin should remain natural and photographic rather than plastic, silicone, waxy, porcelain-like, airbrushed, or digitally synthetic.
PHOTOGRAPHIC RENDERING:
Use the same soft, even, natural studio lighting for this profile as for a clean front-facing portrait of this person. Gentle contrast, soft shadow transitions, no harsh or high-contrast lighting.
Keep the skin surface smooth, intact and even across the whole face, jaw and neck: fine subtle texture only, no granular detail, no rough patches, no scattered dark dots, no clusters of visible pores.
Use restrained sharpening and soft realistic detail. The image should look like a clean modern studio photograph, not a gritty, grainy or over-processed image.
Keep natural true-to-life color, natural skin reflectance and smooth continuous tonal transitions across the face, jawline and neck.
The finished profile must look like it was taken in the same session, with the same camera, the same lens, the same lighting and the same color grading as the person's approved front-facing portrait.
EYEBROWS:
Keep the exact eyebrow character established in the reference.
The eyebrows remain naturally shaped, medium-density, soft-edged and naturally integrated with the skin.
Maintain natural overall hair volume and slightly organic irregularity.
Do not make the eyebrows sparse, overly sharp, overly thick, perfectly shaped, tattoo-like, or individually over-rendered.
HAIR:
Keep the exact same black wavy hairstyle from the reference.
Preserve the same hairline, density, overall volume, silhouette and natural wave pattern.
The hair remains soft, lightweight, naturally wavy and slightly irregular.
Keep loose natural waves with natural direction and airy volume.
The hair should appear clean, soft and naturally arranged, with a matte to soft-satin photographic appearance.
Do not turn the hair into heavy solid blocks, rope-like strands, ribbon-like strands, wet hair, greasy hair, waxed hair, gelled hair, or highly glossy artificial hair.
Only a small amount of very fine natural flyaway hair is visible.
FACIAL HAIR:
Keep the facial hair minimal, clean and low contrast: only very short, sparse hairs around the upper lip and mouth area, with visible skin between the hairs.
Keep the chin and jawline clean and naturally youthful.
Do not create a beard, heavy stubble, beard shadow, sideburns, or dense facial hair.
MOLE:
Preserve the small dark mole at the outer corner of his LEFT eye.
Keep it small, dark and naturally embedded in the skin.
Do not remove, blur, cover or relocate it.
FINAL:
One single natural photograph of the same person, seen from the left side, with a clean and consistent photographic quality matching the approved front-facing portrait.

inputs.text:
Regenerate the image as a natural high-end photographic portrait while preserving the exact identity of the reference person.

Keep him clearly as a 24-year-old young adult man in his early twenties.

Preserve the recognizable identity and overall facial character of the reference. Keep the facial appearance refined, attractive and naturally masculine, with balanced facial proportions and a youthful adult appearance.

Do not exaggerate any particular ethnic facial characteristics. Keep the overall appearance natural, contemporary and faithful to the reference image.

Preserve a youthful adult appearance and youthful facial proportions. He should look like a healthy 24-year-old young adult man, not a teenager and not a mature man in his thirties.

Preserve the exact facial identity and recognizable facial structure of the reference.

The face should have a naturally elongated narrow oval shape. Make the face subtly longer than the previous rendering, with slightly greater vertical facial height while maintaining the same recognizable identity and facial width.

Increase the vertical proportion of the face moderately, especially through the midface and lower face, creating a refined elongated facial silhouette. The face should feel noticeably longer and slightly narrow, but still natural and masculine.

Maintain a slim, refined facial silhouette with gently tapered cheeks and a clean, naturally defined jawline. Keep the jaw relatively narrow without making it overly sharp or V-shaped.

Keep the forehead, midface and lower face naturally proportioned, with enough vertical facial length to preserve the elongated appearance.

Keep the chin proportionate and naturally elongated rather than short, wide or recessed. Do not create an exaggerated pointed chin.

Keep the mouth area refined and naturally proportioned. The lips should sit naturally within the facial profile, with subtle and balanced projection. Keep a refined, understated mouth shape with a natural lip contour. The lips should be moderately sized and naturally defined, with a subtle cupid's bow and a balanced lower lip.

Avoid a protruding mouth, forward-projecting lips, overly full lips, exaggerated lower lip, pouty lips, or excessive lip volume. The mouth should remain naturally integrated into the face. Keep the side profile clean and balanced without pronounced mouth projection.

Keep the under-eye area youthful and natural. Very subtle natural tear troughs are acceptable, but avoid deep tear troughs, pronounced under-eye grooves, hollow under-eyes or strong eye bags.

Keep the nasolabial folds extremely subtle and age-appropriate. Avoid deep nasolabial folds, pronounced smile lines, strong facial creases or mature-looking facial lines.

The entire visible skin surface should have a unified, realistic young-adult skin material.

This realistic skin quality must apply continuously across the entire visible body, not only the face: forehead, cheeks, nose, lips, ears, jawline, chin, neck, throat, collar area, clavicles and any visible upper chest or shoulders.

Treat the face, ears, neck and visible upper body as the same continuous human skin material with consistent photographic rendering.

The skin should feel soft, supple and naturally hydrated, with a fine-grained organic surface rather than a digitally sharpened or rough surface.

Prioritize realistic skin material and natural light interaction over visible pore detail.

The skin should have subtle natural microstructure that is visible only through gentle changes in light and tone, not through exaggerated pores, sharp lines or coarse surface detail.

Use delicate skin micro-variation, subtle tonal transitions, natural subsurface light response, soft skin reflectance and very fine natural surface variation.

Skin should have a soft natural specular response with gentle highlights and smooth transitions between light and shadow.

The skin should not look sharpened, crunchy, gritty, rough, dry, cracked, heavily textured or artificially high-frequency.

Avoid excessive pore visibility. Do not emphasize individual pores as the primary source of realism.

Avoid exaggerated skin grain, harsh micro-contrast, excessive local contrast, oversharpening or artificial clarity.

The realism should come from realistic skin material, subtle light scattering, natural tonal variation and photographic rendering rather than sharpening.

Keep the skin youthful, smooth and healthy while retaining believable natural surface variation.

Keep natural skin translucency and subtle tonal variation across all visible skin. Allow very subtle natural redness and slight tonal differences around the nose, cheeks, ears, lips, neck and upper chest.

The skin should be naturally light and slightly fairer than the previous rendering, with a clean light complexion and subtle neutral-warm undertones.

Keep the skin bright and healthy without making it pale, bleached, porcelain-like or overexposed.

Do not smooth the skin excessively. Do not create airbrushed skin, plastic skin, porcelain skin, waxy skin or beauty-filter skin.

Keep the complexion clean and healthy without acne, acne scars, pitted scars, wrinkles, age spots, melasma, hyperpigmentation, brown patches or dirty-looking discoloration.

Keep the eyebrows naturally dense but realistic, with visible individual eyebrow hairs, fine hair texture, natural hair direction and slightly irregular natural density.

Keep only very subtle short natural facial stubble around the upper lip and sides of the mouth. The moustache area should consist of fine individual hairs with visible separation and visible skin between the hairs.

Keep the chin and lower jaw clean-shaven with visible natural skin texture. No beard on the chin, no chin stubble, no goatee, no beard shadow on the chin or lower jaw.

Keep the facial hair subtle and low contrast, never a solid dark patch.

Keep the black wavy hair soft, airy and naturally voluminous. Preserve naturally separated waves, soft hair groupings and a limited number of fine flyaway hairs.

Hair should have realistic soft hair texture and natural variation. Do not make the hair look wet, oily, glossy, stiff, gelled or glued together.

A single small dark mole is clearly visible at the outer corner of his LEFT eye. The mole is small, round and naturally embedded in the skin. It is a distinctive identity marker and must remain visible. Do not remove, blur, cover or relocate the mole.

Use natural directional photographic lighting rather than perfectly flat studio lighting.

Use a large soft diffused light source from slightly above and to one side of the face and upper body, creating gentle natural gradients of light and shadow across both the face and visible neck.

Extend the same soft directional illumination continuously from the face onto the ears, jawline, neck, throat, clavicles and visible upper chest.

Keep the neck and lower visible skin naturally illuminated with the same realistic photographic quality as the face.

Preserve subtle three-dimensional form through gentle tonal transitions rather than strong contrast.

Keep the lighting soft enough that the skin remains smooth and youthful while still revealing subtle natural material variation.

Avoid completely even frontal illumination, but also avoid harsh side lighting or strong raking light that exaggerates pores, wrinkles, tear troughs, nasolabial folds or skin roughness.

Keep the shadows soft and controlled, with gentle transitions along the nose, cheekbones, jawline and neck.

Maintain realistic highlight rolloff across the forehead, nose, cheekbones, lips, ears, neck and clavicles.

Natural realistic exposure, restrained highlights, soft shadow detail, realistic dynamic range and natural light falloff.

The entire visible skin surface should feel like one continuous real human skin material captured by the same high-quality camera, with consistent texture, tone, reflectance and lighting from the face down through the neck and visible upper body.

Natural high-end photographic realism, realistic male portrait photography, subtle cinematic quality, authentic human facial proportions, realistic skin material, natural hair rendering, realistic individual hairs, natural facial shadows, realistic exposure, realistic dynamic range, sharp but natural photographic detail, shallow depth of field, 35mm film photograph, fine natural film grain, muted cinematic color grading, restrained contrast, documentary photographic realism.

The final result should feel like the same person photographed with a high-end camera under natural professional lighting, not a redesigned face, not a generic model, and not an idealized beauty-filter portrait.
